For a curve $r(t)=x(t)i+y(t)j+z(t)k$, the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ at the point $P(x(t),y(t),z(t))$ is given by

$$
T(t)=\frac{{r}^{′}(t)}{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=0:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+1}\,p(t)) \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+1})\cdot p(t)+\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+1}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(p(t)) \\  & =-\frac{2t}{{({t}^{2}+1)}^{2}}\,p(t)+\frac{1}{{t}^{2}+1}\,{p}^{′}(t) \\ {r}^{′}(0) & =-\frac{2(0)}{{({0}^{2}+1)}^{2}}\,p(0)+\frac{1}{{0}^{2}+1}\,{p}^{′}(0) \\  & =0(2\,i+j-k)+(\,i-2\,j-2k) \\  & =\,i-2\,j-2k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(0):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}‖r(0)‖ & =\sqrt{(1)^{2}+(-2)^{2}+(-2)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize ${r}^{′}(0):$  

$$
\begin{aligned}T(0) & =\frac{{r}^{′}(0)}{‖{r}^{′}(0)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\cdot (i-2\,j-2\,k) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\,i-\frac{2}{3}\,j-\frac{2}{3}\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the unit tangent vector to the curve at the point that corresponds to $t=0$ is  $T(0)=\frac{1}{3}\,i-\frac{2}{3}\,j-\frac{2}{3}\,k.$
